First listed 2025-04-28 · episode or wrap

A Financial Crisis or Just a Bank Stock Correction?

Charles Peabody and Brent Erensel argue banks are better capitalized and reserved while private capital contains the next major risk. Eisman tests that story against sparse disclosure and distinguishes balance-sheet resilience from immediate investment timing. Peabody favors Citi, predicts a summer bank-merger wave, and expects a new S&P low by June. The index forecast failed; Citi's tangible-book outcome roughly matched the likely intended target, while the Banamex IPO window failed. Accounting mechanisms are useful, but claims that private capital is unregulated and reserves eliminate future provisioning are overstated.

YouTube · 2025-04-28 ↗
Eisman's strongest contribution is evidentiary discipline: he challenges opaque private-credit allegations, warns about backward-looking data, and rejects weak political signals. Guest forecasts must remain separate. Primary evidence supports regulatory resilience and several Citi facts but cannot turn modeled recession survival into an observed outcome.

YouTube automatic captions; speaker attribution requires context

Named introductions identify Charles (Charlie) Peabody and Brent Erensel of Portales. Peabody supplies the crisis, market-timing and Citi theses; Erensel gives the Dodd-Frank framing and M&T preference. Attribution of short interjections is inferred from turn context and marked medium where appropriate.

  • Recorded April 23, 2025 after market close; published April 28.
  • Opening 1907 montage repeats later discussion.
  • Automatic captions distort Erensel, CECL, Tarullo, Citi, M&T and NDFI.
  • The $96 Citi book target likely means tangible book, but the speaker does not say so.
  • S&P earnings arithmetic shifts from 275 to 260 and then 240; keep the revised scenario and do not silently repair it.
  • Peabody explicitly labels insurer transfers speculation without supporting data.
  • The medical-device example is unnamed and Stryker is only a tentative guess.
  • Tarullo is incorrectly identified as the original statutory Vice Chair for Supervision.

youtube-M2H_hddVX8I-c006 · explanation

About $10 trillion created through QE flowed directly into private capital and largely bypassed banking.

Wrong
Source · 5:06-6:08 ↗
SpeakerBrent Erensel
Stanceasserted
Horizonnot stated
Materialitymajor

The amount is unverified and the literal plumbing claim is inconsistent with reserve/deposit accounting. Portfolio reallocation is not direct allocation of QE money to funds.

Conditional reasoning

When a central bank purchases a security from a nonbank, settlement credits its bank's reserves and the seller's deposit; when buying from a bank it credits reserves. Neither entry is a direct private-fund capital contribution. Subsequent purchases can change ownership of deposits but do not make all QE equal private-capital inflows.

Assessment test: Trace purchases, bank settlement balances and subsequent investor reallocations.

Evidence and assessment details

Attribution confidence: medium. Assessment confidence: high. Thesis family: qe-direct-private-capital-flow.

No independent empirical outcome evidence is attached. A principle, disclosure or unfinished forecast is not a verified investment win.

Source · 41:45-42:45 ↗

The result follows algebraically, assuming no other changes and the matching book measure.

Conditional reasoning

With equity B, shares N and repurchase q at price P, post-buyback BVPS=(B-qP)/(N-q). This exceeds B/N exactly when P<B/N, for q<N. Tangible book requires its own numerator.

Assessment test: Distinguish ordinary book from tangible book and use actual purchase prices.
